newsitem.title: USA: Clinton budget would fund improvements to GDP data.
newsitem.headline: Clinton budget would fund improvements to GDP data.

text.p: President Clinton's fiscal 1998 budget would provide money to improve statistics on gross domestic product, particularly in the key area of services, Commerce Undersecretary Everett Ehrlich said Thursday.

The White House, citing the need to improve statistics to help them keep up with changing economic developments, has proposed a 15 percent increase in the budget for the Commerce Department's Bureau of Economic Analysis, which produces GDP.

Speaking at a briefing for reporters, Ehrlich said the money would help tackle a problem that many economists see as a major shortcoming of statistics on output -- their failure to fully capture what is happening in the service sector.

If the additional funds are granted, the Commerce Department would be able to improve the measurement of health, finance, telecommunications, retail, insurance and software, which make up about half of total U.S. output, Ehrlich said.

Since economists generally believe U.S. statistics understate overall economic growth in the service area, Ehrlich said the "common presumption" is that the measurement improvements would tend to raise GDP and productivity growth.
He said improvements would take place over the next couple of years if the money is approved by Congress.
